newsitem.title: USA: State Farm sees $150 mln in Hurricane Fran claims.
newsitem.headline: State Farm sees $150 mln in Hurricane Fran claims.

text.p: State Farm Insurance Cos, the largest insurer of homes and cars in the United States, said it expects to pay about $150 million in claims for damage from Hurricane Fran.

State Farm said estimates are very preliminary because the damage is spread over hundreds of miles, primarily in North Carolina, and weekend damage assessments were affected by power outages and flooding. Many areas were not yet accessible because of safety concerns, the company said in a statement.

With an estimated 35,000 home and business claims for $125 million and 10,000 auto claims totaling an estimated $25 million, the expected toll is about one-third as costly to State Farm as Hurricane Hugo was in 1989 ($480 million).
The estimates may change, State Farm said.
"This was a bad storm, particularly in terms of lives lost, but it could have been a lot worse in terms of property damage," State Farm Vice President Frank Haines said in a statement.
